title: Choose independent copies instead of shared names
goal: Compare copies, hard links and symbolic links by type, inode, contents and metadata.
challenge: Preserve an independent before-copy; the teaching original is deliberately changed through its hard link. Create an independent metadata-preserving copy, a hard link and a symlink; demonstrate which objects change when editing the copy and when editing through the hard link. Explain why none replaces versioned backup policy.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/local-copies.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/local-copies.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here
steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace; stop on error and record its absolute path. Reopening boots the disk, not these shell variables. Never use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A new private directory; no pre-existing files are changed.

steps.command: here && fresh original.txt before.txt copy.txt alias.txt pointer && { printf 'baseline\n' > original.txt; chmod 0640 original.txt; cp -p original.txt before.txt; cp -p original.txt copy.txt; ln original.txt alias.txt; ln -s original.txt pointer; }
steps.explanation: Small known regular file; cp -p preserves relevant mode and timestamps, not all possible Linux metadata.
steps.expected: Independent copy versus shared inode versus link text.

steps.command: here && { stat -c '%F %d:%i %h %a %n' original.txt copy.txt alias.txt pointer; stat -Lc '%d:%i %n' pointer; readlink pointer; }
steps.explanation: stat without -L inspects the symlink itself; -L follows it. Do not confuse the two types.
steps.expected: Copy inode differs; alias shares; pointer is a symbolic link.

steps.command: here && { printf 'copy-only\n' >> copy.txt; cmp original.txt before.txt; printf 'shared\n' >> alias.txt; cat original.txt pointer copy.txt before.txt; }
steps.explanation: First change only the copy; then deliberately demonstrate a shared write. Keep the independent before-copy.
steps.expected: Original and pointer show baseline/shared; copy shows baseline/copy-only; before stays baseline.

steps.command: here && { cp -P pointer pointer-copy; test -L pointer-copy; readlink pointer-copy; test "$(stat -c %a copy.txt)" = 640; }
steps.explanation: GNU cp -P copies the symlink object; ordinary cp of a command-line symlink normally follows it. This fixture uses -P explicitly.
steps.expected: Two symlinks with target original.txt; copy mode retained.
